Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le 6-3x-2y},
$$

where $D$ is the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane.

To find the top boundary curve of $D$ in the form $y=y(x),$ we substitute $z=0$ into the equation $z=6-3x-2y:$

$$
0=6-3x-2y\,⟹\,y=3-\frac{3}{2}x
$$

Then, we have

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 3-\frac{3}{2}x},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064036/assets/8b3edbf61dc8a2b2a027c79a0ac1bbee54163b89277040119aaea382121998ff.png)

Hence, the type I representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le 3-\frac{3}{2}x,\,\,0\le z\le 6-3x-2y}.
$$

Therefore, the volume of $R$ is given by the following triple integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3-3x/2}{\int }_{0}^{6-3x-2y}dz\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3-3x/2}[z]_{z=0}^{z=6-3x-2y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3-3x/2}(6-3x-2y)-0\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3-3x/2}6-3x-2y\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[(6-3x)y-{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=3-3x/2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}((6-3x)(3-\frac{3x}{2})-{(3-\frac{3x}{2})}^{2})-0\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(3-\frac{3x}{2})((6-3x)-(3-\frac{3x}{2}))\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(3-\frac{3x}{2})(3-\frac{3x}{2})\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{(3-\frac{3x}{2})}^{2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}9-9x+\frac{9{x}^{2}}{4}\,dx \\  & ={[9x-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{3{x}^{3}}{4}]}_{x=0}^{x=2} \\  & =(9(2)-\frac{9(2)^{2}}{2}+\frac{3(2)^{3}}{4})-0 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
